title: Checks for unnecessary pass statements and ellipsis (...) literals in functions, classes, and other blocks.
summary: In Python, the pass statement and ellipsis (...) literal serve as placeholders, allowing for syntactically correct empty code blocks. The primary purpose of these nodes is to avoid syntax errors in situations where a statement or expression is syntactically required, but no code needs to be executed. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for duplicate field definitions in classes.
summary: Defining a field multiple times in a class body is redundant and likely a mistake. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.208.
message_templates: Class field `{}` is defined multiple times

title: Checks for enums that contain duplicate values.
summary: Enum values should be unique. Non-unique values are redundant and likely a mistake. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.224.

title: Checks for unnecessary dictionary unpacking operators (**).
summary: Unpacking a dictionary into another dictionary is redundant. The unpacking operator can be removed, making the code more readable. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.231.

title: Checks for unnecessary dict kwargs.
summary: If the dict keys are valid identifiers, they can be passed as keyword arguments directly, without constructing unnecessary dictionary. This also makes code more type-safe as type checkers often cannot precisely verify dynamic keyword arguments. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.231.

title: Checks for lambdas that can be replaced with the list or dict builtins.
summary: Using container builtins are more succinct and idiomatic than wrapping the literal in a lambda. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.208.

title: Checks for range calls with an unnecessary start argument.
summary: range(0, x) is equivalent to range(x), as 0 is the default value for the start argument. Omitting the start argument makes the code more concise and idiomatic. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.286.

title: Checks for startswith or endswith calls on the same value with different prefixes or suffixes.
summary: The startswith and endswith methods accept tuples of prefixes or suffixes respectively. Passing a tuple of prefixes or suffixes is more efficient and readable than calling the method multiple times. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-pie and made it stable in v0.0.243.
